reviews.concern: staged-file quality gate parsed from the contract
reviews.rationale: One fail-closed hook: parse QUALITY.md, ignore, baseline, and reviews, then apply size, name, and root rules. Splitting parser from checks would let a partial gate go green.

reviews.concern: board App event loop and selection
reviews.rationale: App owns snapshots, selection, overlay, refresh queue, error backoff, and input. Keys, a second click (detail), footer-key clicks, timer retry, and r-reload all mutate the same selected_id and overlay; extracting one handler would split that state.

paint, pack_chrome, hit_at, and footer share ScanView, scroll_row, and snapshot order so table vs cards stay one board. Hit::Row and Hit::Key use that same chrome; extracting footer hits would desync pager, click, and body height.

These tests drive one App.draw path for packed columns, monthly remaining, prepaid section, empty/unsigned rows, selected-row highlight, footer clicks, and the t card toggle. Splitting would duplicate mixed_app bootstrap and hide column-alignment regressions.

These tests drive one App through keys, mouse, overlays, live-config reload, and error backoff retry. Card clicks may open detail, so oracles dismiss that overlay. Splitting would duplicate mixed_app bootstrap and hide selection regressions.
One suite maps vendor JSON into domain status with shared helpers. Per-vendor files already exist for large adapters; remaining cases stay here so mapper regressions share one harness.
One generator writes the submodule register and the four sidecar files from .gitmodules. Splitting the bash wrapper from the writer would let the register and the sidecars disagree.

One fail-closed checker for agent files: presence, caps, chain links, memory shape, submodule register and dirtiness. Splitting parser from checks would let a partial gate go green and stop matching the commit dispatcher.

reviews.concern: agent-kit chain and growth classification library
reviews.rationale: Shared primitives for crowd counting, chain parsing, kit-root detection, submodule pruning and ignore handling. Every kit gate imports these; splitting them would let the chain, growth and status tools disagree about what a product folder is.

One vendor module: CLI/keychain token resolution, the Responses SSE remaining mapper, the 429 exhausted mapper, and the Provider impl. They share the Muse request/response contract; splitting token lookup from mapping would scatter one vendor's wire shape across files.

reviews.concern: accounts.toml registry: model, parser, and init template
reviews.rationale: One concern: the AccountRow/Vendor model, the toml parser and its validation (inline-key refusal, account cap, id/label uniqueness), and the commented init template the user edits. The template and the parser are the same contract; splitting them would let the visible template and the accepted schema drift apart.
